summary.headline: Summary of household mail statistics for fiscal year 2025.

statements.text: For all households, the metric all household mail per household was 637.3 pieces per household per year in FY2025, falling by 44.7 pieces per household per year from the previous year across the FY2025 methodology break, and falling by 199.7 pieces per household per year from 5 years earlier across the FY2024 and FY2025 methodology breaks.

caveats: Beginning in 2010, diary data were restated because of changes in weighting methodology (Appendix A8 table notes). Values before 2010 use the earlier weighting.

From the FY2024 report, results are published as pieces per household per year, and the survey contractor changed (NuStats to RCF). The FY2024 report restated 2014-2023 on its own basis, so its values for those years can differ slightly from earlier reports (e.g. bills paid by mail in 2014: 34% in FY2023, 33% in FY2024).

FY2025 used a new survey design (renamed the Household Mail Survey); Q1 was still covered by the old survey. Age bands changed to Under 45 / 45-64 / 65+ (previously 18-34 / 35-54 / 55+), and 'Large MSA' was redefined in January 2025 from the top 30 metros to metros of 1 million or more.

summary.headline: Comparative summary of household mail per household across reporting years

statements.text: For All households, all household mail per household fell by 437.4 pieces per household per year from 2014 to 2025 across the FY2024 and FY2025 methodology breaks.
For All households, all household mail per household decreased by 403.3 pieces per household per year from 2015 to 2025 across the FY2024 and FY2025 methodology breaks.
For All households, all household mail per household declined by 199.7 pieces per household per year from 2020 to 2025 across the FY2024 and FY2025 methodology breaks.
For All households, all household mail per household dropped by 44.7 pieces per household per year from 2024 to 2025 across the FY2025 methodology break.

caveats: Beginning in 2010, diary data were restated because of changes in weighting methodology.
From the FY2024 report, results are published as pieces per household per year, and the survey contractor changed from NuStats to RCF.
FY2025 used a new survey design renamed the Household Mail Survey, with changes to age bands and the definition of Large MSA.
Projections need at least 8 consecutive annual values; this series has fewer, so none is shown.
